intended_object: A Hermitian (self-adjoint) square matrix: A equals its conjugate transpose Aᴴ, i.e. A_{ji}^* = A_{ij} for all i, j. Over the reals (trivial star) this means a symmetric matrix. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body `Aᴴ = A` is the definition of a Hermitian matrix, where `Aᴴ` is the conjugate transpose, i.e. the transpose with `star` applied to each entry. Defining a conjugate transpose only needs a `Star` structure on the entries, so working over any type with `Star α` and any index type `n` is the most general setting. With the trivial star on ℝ (or on any commutative ring with trivial star), the condition reduces to symmetry, which is what the docstring says. The general Mathlib notion `IsSelfAdjoint A` (`star A = A`, using the star structure on matrices) is equivalent; Mathlib proves this as `Matrix.isHermitian_iff_isSelfAdjoint`. So this is a specialised name for that notion, not a narrower one. There is no degenerate-case problem: when `n` is empty, every matrix is Hermitian, as it should be.
